swap_order_repeat.what_did_not: BOTH performance claims. (1) The prefill -47%: swapped order, dspark's prefill BEAT control (15.9 vs 11.0 tok/s) - the regression was a boot-order/host-cache artifact, not the drafter. CLAIM DROPPED. (2) The decode +29%: same arm, same acceptance, verify passes cost 166.8 ms today vs 104.0 ms on 2026-10-25 (draft 9.9 both days) - today the same MTP is 22% SLOWER than its control. CLAIM DOWNGRADED to 'accepted 1.984 tokens/pass deterministically; wall-clock benefit not established'.
swap_order_repeat.pattern: within each session the FIRST boot's prefill ran faster (39.2 then 15.9) than the SECOND's (20.7 then 11.0) regardless of which arm booted first; between sessions the first boot of 2026-10-26 (15.9) was far slower than 2026-10-25's (39.2, hours after same-model witnesses had warmed the GGUF page cache while vLLM was NOT resident). The box's ~110 GiB vLLM residency poisons the model's page cache between witness days; single-pair n=1 boots cannot separate arm from order from cache state on this engine.
swap_order_repeat.rule_for_future_perf_witnesses: any perf claim on this engine needs SAME-SESSION repeated boots per arm (control,arm,control,arm minimum) and must report the within-arm spread alongside the arm means; a single pair supports only the deterministic invariants (counts, acceptance, path statistics), never a rate comparison.
